title: Learning without inward turning stays trapped in Maya
subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 86
summary: The shabad begins by criticizing scholars who read and shout while remaining attached to Maya. It pushes further by exposing teaching without contemplation and ends in the waste of a life spent repeating what was never inwardly recognized.
whyItMatters: This shabad speaks to the part of us that hides inside religious language, intellect, or correction. Taken seriously, it strips away borrowed authority and asks whether the heart has actually turned.
takeaway: Knowledge without inward freedom still serves attachment.

lines.gurmukhi: ਪੰਡਿਤੁ ਪੜਿ ਪੜਿ ਉਚਾ ਕੂਕਦਾ ਮਾਇਆ ਮੋਹਿ ਪਿਆਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: pa(n)ddit paR paR uchaa kookadhaa maiaa moh piaar ||
lines.translation: The Pandits, the religious scholars, read and read, and shout out loud, but they are attached to the love of Maya.

lines.gurmukhi: ਅੰਤਰਿ ਬ੍ਰਹਮੁ ਨ ਚੀਨਈ ਮਨਿ ਮੂਰਖੁ ਗਾਵਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: a(n)tar braham na cheeniee man moorakh gaavaar ||
lines.translation: They do not recognize God within themselves-they are so foolish and ignorant!

lines.gurmukhi: ਦੂਜੈ ਭਾਇ ਜਗਤੁ ਪਰਬੋਧਦਾ ਨਾ ਬੂਝੈ ਬੀਚਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: dhoojai bhai jagat parabodhadhaa naa boojhai beechaar ||
lines.translation: In the love of duality, they try to teach the world, but they do not understand meditative contemplation.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬਿਰਥਾ ਜਨਮੁ ਗਵਾਇਆ ਮਰਿ ਜੰਮੈ ਵਾਰੋ ਵਾਰ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: birathaa janam gavaiaa mar ja(n)mai vaaro vaar ||1||
lines.translation: They lose their lives uselessly; they die, only to be re-born, over and over again. ||1||

structure: The shabad begins by exposing scholarship still chained to Maya.
From there it shows how easily teaching the world can become another form of duality.
The closing movement rests by naming the cost: a life spent repeating what was never inwardly known.
